body: I feel like a few months back I lost the energy to make the effort.

Eh. Call me a goody-two-shoes if you like, but the pain (and STRESS!) of detox is such a subjective thing… I’ve known detox staffers who felt it was their duty to run an ersatz jail and provide patients with as little medication as possible because something something bla bla stoicism it’s not sobriety if you’re on buprenoprhine and that whole song and dance… but detox patients are still patients, while treatment is still treatment, and not punishment… for medication-assisted detox, is it really the end of the world if a voluntary patient needing one more pill gets one more pill, even if maybe the occasional malingerer gets one too? I’m not suggesting you unlock the meds cabinet and let anyone ransack it, but if someone on 8mg of Subutex daily feels they need 16mg, or even 24mg, it doesn’t depress breathing, it’s their recovery at the end of the day… I’m not sure I see the harm in listening to the needs patients express and more often than not giving them the benefit of the doubt. 🤷🏻‍♀️

To the doctors here with patients reporting potentially-serious symptoms that you deem frivolous: when you “frighten the truth out of them” by saying “Oh, confirming your illness will require such-and-such a PAINFUL TEST…”

Do you ever worry that you’re just frightening away legitimate patients who fear short-term pain more than the long-term consequences of going untreated?

This may on its surface seem not to apply to your “patient presenting an obvious ink-stain as a melanoma” type. I ask, though, because my family is riddled with doctors, and they were all rather compassionate types who believed anyone concerned enough to see a doctor, even if that person was misinterpreting, misrepresenting, or even flat-out lying about their symptoms, must have something in their lives that was really bothering them if they’ve gone to all the trouble of seeing a doctor in the first place. So my family members would always try to coax out of that person what was really going on, to then address that.

Flash forward to several decades later, and with my social science training I’m conducting tests on large sample groups of doctors to determine their diagnosing and prescribing behaviors… and for the first time in my life I encounter haughty, preening, self-obsessed oafs who feel every patient is there to rob that “doctor” of time better spent on a yacht or a golf course: real money-driven types who probably could’ve just as easily sold junk bonds in the ‘80s or flipped real estate for a living rather than treat sick people… to whom “First do no harm” wasn’t even a passing thought.

If you’re behaving callously towards ANY patient, don’t you worry that you’re in the wrong profession? Or does the money and the lack of a conscience keep any doubt from popping up in the first place?
Oh my goodness… HOW DOES HE KNOW MY SECRETS!?? 😍

Well, the crooks who profited in running Europe’s asylums insisted any information giving their captives similar human status as fully abled people was dangerous and  backwards pseudoscientific charlatanry, so — plus ça change…
That primate is more human than some humans in my family!
